messages:
Rashid: Handoff from night shift — quick summary:
- No active incidents.
- Tenant X experienced a brief 5m latency spike around 01:12 UTC (p95 from 180ms -> 430ms). It auto-resolved after the cache-worker restarted (see below).
- Deployed lightweight patch to cache worker to add defensive null check (deployed to staging + canary at 02:05 UTC). No rollback needed.
- DB replica lag peaked at ~22s for a few minutes during nightly index maintenance; replicas caught up. Watch replica lag.

What to watch:
- p95 latency for api-prod (esp /v1/generate) — keep an eye on Grafana dashboard 'prod-api-latency' for any reappearance of the 400ms spikes.
- Replica lag alert: slo/db-replica-lag (threshold 30s) — if it fires, check `pg_repl_status` and open a pager.
- Cache-worker restarts: if >3 restarts in 30m, that's actionable — see runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/cache-worker-restart

Action items for today's shift:
- Leah: follow up with infra to confirm nightly index job window is adjusted (they scheduled 02:00-02:30 UTC). Please confirm by EOD.
- Kevin: keep an eye on canary rollout for the new batching config (rolling to 20% at 04:00 UTC). If errors spike >0.5% on canary, pause and ping infra.
- Anna: lift the post-deploy smoke tests for embeddings and text-gen after 06:00 UTC.

Notes + context:
- Root cause for latency spike looks like a pathological cache key growth from a customer testing high-cardinality prompts. We've throttled their 2 heavy routes and added a temporary cache TTL reduction.
- The null-check patch prevents a rare NPE when cache item serialization length is zero. Patch id: patch/cache-nullcheck-202503. Deployed to canary + prod canaries.

Logs/snippets used during triage:
```
# observed in cache-worker logs
2025-03-23T01:12:07Z ERROR cache.worker serialize: zero-length payload, key="user:acct:1234:ctx"
2025-03-23T01:12:07Z INFO cache.worker restarting worker pid=4321
```

Rashid: I'm handing off now — I'm available on DMs for 30m if anyone needs context. :wave:

Leah: Thanks — quick Q: do we have the customer id for that high-cardinality test? I want to block their routes at the ingress level if needed.

Rashid: Yes, cust_08942. I've already added a temporary ingress rule to throttle their calls to /v1/generate to 10rps. I'll drop the rule once infra confirms index window moved.

Kevin: Acknowledge. I'll watch canary errors and set an alert in slack if >0.3% for 10m. Can you share the dashboard panel?

Rashid: Panel link: https://grafana.redwood/prod/api-latency?panelId=7 — p95 is the key metric.

Anna: Noted on smoke tests. Planning to run them at ~06:10 UTC. If anything fails, will create a short incident and ping oncall.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout started (batching-config-v2) — 5% -> 20% over 20m. ID: deploy-20250323-1912

oncall-bot: Reminder: daily handoff checklist not completed: confirm DB maintenance window (Leah).

Leah: Will confirm with infra now and update here. Thanks for the handoff, Rashid.

Kevin: I'm taking the next 4-hour block for oncall coverage. If you need me for escalation after that, ping in #eng-oncall and DM.

Rashid: Thanks all — leaving notes in the ticket: https://redwood.internal/tickets/INC-arch-789 (non-incident follow-up).
